A single eye blinks away salty grit and a sigh bubbles up from the wet sand. Half submerged on the beach, the gharril looks to the shore waiting, while 
the rising tide crashes on its shell. A pack of vinnirex leap and play on the sand, two young pups fighting over a violet branch of coral that broke off from 
a recent storm. More bubbles escape the maw of the large snail as its patience wears thin. The sun sets further, the sky overhead spreads crimson and the 
waters continue to rise. With a splash, the much chewed upon coral branch lands near the awaiting cerrophol. With an instinct built on eons of success, 
its large eye recedes into the soft flesh of its face to look like just any outcropping of coral. With a yap and bark, one of the young canines paddle out to 
retrieve their toy, only for four grasping tentacle-like appendages to burst out of the water and grip the small furred mammal. With one last bark, it is 
pulled under, and the rising tide covers the top of the snail's twisted shell.
By the rise and fall of the tide, the creatures of the coast prowl this highly competitive stretch of habitable land that shifts wildly between 
dawn and dusk leaves little room for calm herbivores, and instead plays host to a constant struggle between scavengers. As the receding 
waves expose long stretches of coral reefs that after eons have expanded past the waves to crawl onto land like questing, outstretched 
fingers, many of the advantageous, amphibious creatures stalk out to claim trapped prey. With the telltale sound of a slapping fin, a 
fish trapped in a tidal pool calls to the chitinous horde of crustaceans and slithering cephalopod that are found teeming on nearly every 
stretch of sand around the island. Striding above the wave of smaller beasts, illithisk, cerrophol and gharril compete for the morsel 
of flesh, their struggle often leading to one of their kind being left in the sand for the scurrying scavengers to feast on instead. As this 
competition carries ever onward like the ebb and flow of the tide, a lone slannethiss lifts its sensory horns into the salted air, awaiting 
larger, more worthy prey. Out beyond the beach, wide swathes of coral border much of the island, these colorful bone-like columns are 
covered in urchins, mollusks and smaller corals. Like darting birds among trees, spiera shoals weave in and out of the branching coral 
snatching fish with ease, giving the long daellash a wide berth, with their wide mouths snapping at any passing prey. Further out still, 
tread arkiopti, sharped stones slicing through the air as they aim to fell a gliding tiama while a goliarch rushes upward to eviscerate the 
lone large crustacean. There is no peace among the flora and fauna that struggle to survive the crashing waves, and the Strands offer 
no easy welcoming to Travelers.

nearly living material. The dome-like structure is made of layers of calcium

withstand damage by radiating out the blunt force energy outwards into its

as its home, and can spend years chewing through the same coral plate, slowly 
killing it while excavating a nest for its spawn
